environment.description: FastAPI service deployed on ECS Fargate behind an AWS ALB configured with mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication. The ALB HTTPS:443 listener has MutualAuthentication mode set to 'verify' with a trust store referencing an internal PKI CA bundle (arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:truststore/internal-pki-ca/ts-0abc123def456). Connection attempts without a valid client certificate signed by the internal CA are rejected at the TLS handshake level (ALB returns HTTP 400 before forwarding). The trust store contains only the intermediate CA used to issue certificates to registered internal microservices. Certificate revocation is checked via CRL hosted in S3. Additionally, the ALB access logs show that the X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number header is populated for all forwarded requests, confirming mTLS negotiation completed. The target group health check path is /health on port 8080. No WAF is attached. The service container runs with the same configuration as the exploitable environment.

config.alb_listener: HTTPS:443 with ACM certificate, MutualAuthentication: {mode: verify, trustStoreArn: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456789012:truststore/internal-pki-ca/ts-0abc123def456, ignoreClientCertificateExpiry: false}
config.trust_store: Contains only intermediate CA 'Internal Services CA G2' - issues certs to registered service identities only
config.crl_check: enabled, CRL from s3://internal-pki-crl/services-ca-g2.crl refreshed every 60s
config.authentication: mTLS at ALB layer - no additional application-level auth
config.network: public subnet, NAT gateway for outbound, no network ACL restrictions on egress
config.container: python:3.11-slim, no seccomp profile, default capabilities
